scope: Every raised air intake sold for the JB74, plus the cyclone pre-cleaner heads that clamp onto one, plus what is actually on sale in Taiwan. Compiled for a 3D configurator, so silhouette and geometry matter more than marketing copy.

Measure that in pixels and the rest of the photo scales from it.

rules.text: CONFIRMED - the JB74's airbox is on the RIGHT of the engine bay, and every snorkel made for the car runs the RIGHT A-pillar. No maker offers a left-hand version and none claims one. Bravo's own installation guide has a 'FITMENT SIDE: Right' header on page 1; URNIETA's fitting steps begin by removing the right-side A-pillar corner cover; ARB's Torqit listing names the driver's-side guard (Australia is RHD). The same kit serves LHD and RHD cars - Bravo's install video states the SSJN is 'valid for all engine versions and LHD & RHD' - because the airbox does not move with the steering wheel. The configurator's existing assumption is therefore correct, including app.html's rule that the A-pillar pods shift to the left when a snorkel is fitted.

On a naturally-aspirated petrol JB74 a raised air intake buys LESS than most listings imply, and the honest breakdown is worth carrying in the UI. (1) WATER: it removes ONE failure mode - water going straight down the intake and hydro-locking the engine, which is the expensive one. It does NOT make the car amphibious, because the intake is not the first thing to flood. Suzuki publishes no wading depth for the JB74 at all; what floods first on a stock car is the axle, transfer and gearbox BREATHERS, whose stock hoses terminate low in the engine bay - the fact that FOUR different makers sell a JB74 breather-extension kit - ARB, TJM, Harrop, and Oz Jimny's own 'No Drill' Differential Breather Adaptor Kit V2 - is the clearest evidence that fitting a snorkel alone leaves the job half done. After the breathers come the alternator, the starter, the cabin floor and the door seals. A snorkel is one item on a wading checklist, not the checklist. (2) DUST: this is the benefit owners actually feel, and it applies every dry weekend rather than once a year. The intake moves from inside the engine bay to roof height, above the dust cloud the car's own wheels throw up, which is why cyclone pre-cleaner heads exist - Donaldson publishes 75% separation for its plain cyclone and 99% (ISO 5011 / SAE J726) for the TopSpin, all of it dust the paper element never has to see. (3) POWER: essentially nothing. The 'ram air' framing is marketing. At Taiwanese road and trail speeds the dynamic pressure recovered is negligible, a snorkel ADDS length and bends to the intake tract, and the K15B is naturally aspirated with no intercooler for cooler air to help. One installer's own honest wording is 'a marginal gain in response'. (4) A REAL COST: intake resonance. A long hard tube up the pillar can drone - there is a published owner video specifically about a Bravo-fitted Jimny's 'harmonic resonance issue'. Worth saying out loud in a configurator, because it is the complaint that surprises people. (5) THE STRONGEST SOURCE ON ALL OF THIS IS A SELLER. Torqit, who will happily sell you an AUD 1,690 JB74 snorkel: 'A snorkel does not turn your vehicle into a submarine. It protects the air intake, but safe water crossings still depend on good preparation. Your vehicle still has electrical components, transmission and differential breathers, door seals, bearings and other parts that may be affected by water.' And Safari's own FAQ on factory raised intakes: 'Factory snorkels are often designed for styling rather than for performance, and most are Raised Air Intakes thus not watertight.' (6) SAFARI GRADES ITS OWN RANGE THE SAME WAY: V-SPEC is sold as MAINTAINING factory-level airflow, and only the 4-inch ARMAX claims 'up to 70% more airflow'. A standard snorkel does not add flow - the maker says so. If flow is the goal, the part that moves the needle is the AIRBOX: AVO Turboworld claims >4 kW at the wheels for its sealed JB74 airbox and larger intake tube, on the grounds that the factory throttle hose makes turbulence, and Torqit likewise sells its stainless airbox as the flow product and the snorkel as the protection product. (7) BE HONEST ABOUT THE EVIDENCE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. There is no dyno test of any snorkel on this car, in either direction. There is no published dust-ingestion comparison between a roof-height and a guard-height intake - Donaldson's impressive figures are for FILTRATION, not intake height. Suzuki publishes no wading depth for the JB74 in any market (the Australian spec sheet gives only the 36/27/47-degree angles and 210 mm clearance), so the widely repeated '300 mm' has no traceable source and must never be quoted as a spec. And the JB74's alternator height, ECU location and cooling-fan type could not be established from any reachable source, so do not claim which one floods first. (8) A SNORKEL ADDS RISKS OF ITS OWN: leaking joints, a forward-facing head scooping water in heavy rain, condensate. The makers' countermeasures - drain slots, Torqit's rear-facing mouth, duckbill drain valves in the airbox floor, Donaldson water evacuators - are themselves the evidence those risks are real. Snorkel socks clog in about 45 minutes of dusty driving; Safari only recommends them below 40 km/h with daily cleaning. (9) DIESEL vs PETROL: the whole snorkel industry's argument is written for diesels, which hydro-lock on much less water because of high compression and small clearance volume. The K15B is more tolerant of a small ingestion - a difference of degree, not immunity. And 'no intercooler so it's pointless' does not hold: an intercooler sits downstream of a turbo and is not on the path water takes in. Intake HEIGHT and sealing are the only things that decide whether water gets swallowed.

TAIWAN - a snorkel IS legal, does NOT need a 變更登記, and does NOT have to come off at 驗車, PROVIDED it does not exceed the vehicle height and width recorded on the 行照. That is not an inference: it is a 交通部公路總局 ruling of 2023-03-17, and the 交通部 confirmed it in writing on 2023-04-12 in its reply to the public e-petition 「吉普車強化升級檢驗變更」 (5,276 signatures): 「涉水管及車外附加燈光(工作燈或聚光燈)之變更部分，本部公路總局已研訂檢驗實務認定標準，供檢驗單位據以辦理」. The ruling's four conditions, as published by the petitioners (臺灣極地救援聯盟): the snorkel must be a 模組化套件 - a bought kit, not a shop fabrication - it must be 安裝牢固, it is 不列入車體結構 (not counted as body structure and NOT counted toward vehicle height), and it 不得超過車高及車寬的限制. Result: 可合法驗車，也無需變更登記. STATUTORY BACKING: 第23條 requires registration for changes to 車身式樣 and the rest, but the operative list is its 附件十五, which is EXHAUSTIVE - and the words 涉水管, 呼吸管 and 進氣 do not appear in it once. For contrast a winch sits in point 3 and a ROOF RACK in point 1, the strictest (VSCC structural 審驗 plus registration). A snorkel is in none of the four points, so it was never declared a registrable modification at all. 第23-1條's prohibited list does not reach it either: the engine prohibitions are limited to 機械或渦輪增壓系統 and 氮氣導入裝置, the body ones to 車身外附加燈飾 and lamp tinting. Note the trap next door though - a supercharger or turbo IS prohibited, so a snorkel fitted alongside one of the JB74 supercharger kits sold here inherits that problem, and the snorkel is not what fails. THE 外部突出物 RED HERRING: 車輛安全檢測基準 附件七十七 (M1 車外突出, harmonised with UN R26) and 附件七十八 (N-class, UN R61) are 附表 to 第14條 of the 車輛型式安全審驗管理辦法, whose 第2條 defines that 審驗 as applying 車輛申請新領牌照前 and whose 第3條 binds only manufacturers, body builders and importers. THEY DO NOT BIND AN OWNER'S RETROFIT and are not a periodic-inspection item. Confirming it, VSCC's 使用中車輛變更審驗 list has only 7 items and a snorkel is not one. 第39-1條 (定期檢驗, 27 items) has no 突出物 item at all - its only external item is #7 「車輛尺度、顏色、車身式樣與紀錄相符」 - and the single 突出物 mention in 第39條 is confined to item 23, towed trailers. WHERE IT ACTUALLY FAILS: REGISTERED HEIGHT. The absolute ceiling is irrelevant - 第38條 caps a small car at 1.5x its width or 2.85 m, so a 1645 mm-wide JB74 may legally be 2467 mm tall against an actual 1725 mm. What bites is item #7, 車輛尺度與紀錄相符. Owners report a tolerance of about 2 cm and that the measuring rigs tightened from July 2024 (PTT car, 2024-10-21: 「原本登記 173 目前 168 只有 2 公分的容許範圍…7 月後設備更新 車高精度準確」). So a snorkel whose crown clears the roofline - the Torqit hairpin and the Ironman scoop both do - moves from 'nobody's problem' to 'height does not match the 行照', which is the one failure mode with a written rule, an instrument and precedent behind it. EMISSIONS DO NOT CARE: 空污法 第37條's 空氣污染防制設備 list is an exhaustive 14 items (catalyst, EGR, canister, PCV, thermal reactor, secondary air, O2 sensor, deceleration control, DPF, OBD, ECU and so on) and intake ducting is not among them. The only real emissions risk is a badly sealed install drawing false air and wrecking the CO/HC reading - mechanical, not legal. HOW MUCH THIS IS ARGUED ABOUT IN PRACTICE: almost not at all. PTT car / Off-road / CarShop return ZERO threads for 呼吸管; Mobile01 has no dedicated thread; and most tellingly the inspectors' own public forum 「汽車檢驗員資料庫」 returns ZERO hits for both 呼吸管 and 涉水管 while a control search (太陽能板) returns one. Not a single report of a snorkel being ordered off or failing 驗車 was found anywhere. The only owner discussion located is a 2026-08-10 post in the New Jimny JB74 Taiwan Club asking whether a snorkel has to come off, answered 「呼吸管已符合法規唯獨不能超過車頂所規定之高度」 - which matches the 2023 ruling exactly. THE ONE CAVEAT TO CARRY: the 檢驗實務認定標準 itself has never been published. 交通部行政解釋查詢 returns 0 results for both 涉水管 and 呼吸管, it is not in 附件十五, and VSCC does not list it. It is an internal circular to the 監理所 with no citable document number, so an owner has nothing to put in front of an inspector who disagrees. CUTTING THE FENDER: no Taiwanese rule addresses it. 附件十五's only sheet-metal clause covers 廂式平頭小貨車, not passenger cars; 第23-1條 does not prohibit panel work; and a front-fender pass-through does not touch the VIN stamping location (第39-1條 item 1). Whether a grommeted hole counts as a 車身式樣 change is unwritten and entirely the inspector's eye. If it were ever treated as an unreported equipment change the penalties are 處罰條例 第16條 NT$900-1,800 or 第18條 NT$2,400-9,600. WHAT TO TELL AN OWNER: buy a bought kit rather than a shop fabrication, mount it solidly, KEEP THE TOP BELOW THE ROOFLINE, and fit it AFTER the car is plated - 新領牌照檢驗 compares against the 車輛型式安全審驗合格證明書 rather than the 行照, and 車輛型式安全審驗管理辦法 第5條第6款 catches a dealer who modifies a car before plating.

There is NO Safari snorkel and NO ARB-branded snorkel for the JB74, and there never has been. ARB's full product sitemap (11,429 product URLs, read 2026-09-22) carries exactly one Safari snorkel for any Suzuki - SS820HF, for the pre-2012-facelift JB43 - and nothing at all for JB74, JB64 or Sierra. Safari's own site lists only the 1998-2012 1.3L Jimny. ARB owns Safari, and it fills the JB74 gap by reselling TORQIT under ARB part numbers SN02SS and SN02MB. Any listing that says 'Safari snorkel for JB74' is wrong about either the brand or the car.

SS1130HF is NOT a Jimny part. ARB's catalogue gives it as 'Safari V-Spec Snorkel, Jeep Cherokee KJ with 2.4L or 3.7L engine'. SS1130HP does not exist in the ARB catalogue at all - it is not a real part number. Do not carry either against a Jimny.

Three more brands that do NOT make a JB74 snorkel, each checked against the maker's own catalogue. RIVAL 4X4 does not make snorkels for any vehicle: its sitemap has zero 'snorkel' URLs and its categories are bumpers, skid plates, roof racks and winch mounts. DOBINSONS does make snorkels but has no Suzuki entry of any kind - the range covers Ford, Holden, Isuzu, Jeep, Mazda, Mitsubishi, Nissan, Toyota and VW only (useful side fact: its replacement heads come in 77, 85 and 90 mm). APIO returns 'no results' for both シュノーケル and スノーケル and has no air-intake category at all. Do not offer any of the three for this car.

Every JB74 snorkel is in one of two install families, and they look completely different on the car. (1) CUT THE GUARD - the classic Australian/European pattern: a hole is cut in the right front fender's outer skin, a template and usually a grommet or pinch-weld are in the box, and the body starts low on the fender and climbs the entire A-pillar, standing clearly proud of it. Ironman ISNORKEL070, Torqit SN02SS, TJM Airtec, Bravo SSJN, the Taiwanese FRP units and every Chinese generic are in this family. (2) NO CUT, NO DRILL - the body REPLACES a factory trim panel instead: URNIETA's Salado replaces the black hood/fender-top garnish strip, Mega Jimny's Supa-Sleek replaces the A-pillar and cowl trim. These hug the body and are far less visible. Only TWO products are genuinely in family 2. Bravo is NOT one of them, despite how its Australian retailer titles it. WHAT THE CUT ACTUALLY IS, for anyone modelling the hole: Safari's own procedure for this class of part is mark the template, drill 4 mm pilot holes, open with an 83 mm HOLE SAW, extend with an air saw, deburr, touch up the paint against rust, then drill four 8 mm holes in the A-pillar for the brackets. The Brazilian template sold in Taiwan gives the same hole as an oval about 110 mm long with R30 corners, aligned off an existing factory hole in the fender. So the guard opening is roughly 83-110 mm across and the A-pillar carries four small fixings, typically hidden behind the snorkel body.

Bravo's SSJN is sold in Australia as a 'Complete No-Modification Snorkel Kit' and that title is misleading. Bravo's own installation guide PDF (BRAVO_SNORKEL_SUZUKI_JIMNY_Installation_Guide_SSJN.pdf, linked from the retailer's page) carries the step callouts 'Remove', 'Bend', 'Drill', 'Cut' and 'Relocate', and a footnote 'Remove the car's bonnet to install the snorkel'. The kit contains two M6x14 rivnuts, which only exist to be set into a drilled panel. THE GUARD IS CUT. Treat the retailer's title as a sales label, not a fitting fact.

89 mm (3.5 inch) is the de-facto interface diameter at the top of a JB74 snorkel, which is why heads and cyclone pre-cleaners swap across brands. Bravo's guide lists part 2 as 'Snorkel head 89 mm / 3,5"'; Torqit's entire tube is 88.9 mm; jimnybits sells its pre-cleaner as a 3.5 in fitting; Donaldson's cyclones for this class come in 89 mm and 102 mm. The exceptions are Mega Jimny's Supa-Sleek (2 in / 50.8 mm stainless pipework, concealed, no external head at all) and URNIETA (about 80 mm at the collar). For modelling, 89 mm is the number to use for the visible spigot.

Whether a head rotates comes down to one thing: is the joint a round spigot with a band clamp, or moulded in? Bravo's head is a separate 89 mm elbow held by a 'Black clamp' (part 3 in its own kit list), so it turns a full 360 degrees and lifts off. Ironman's upper goose-neck is joined by a visible band clamp, so it can be indexed on assembly - inferred from the photo, not published. URNIETA ships TWO heads, a standard one and a cyclone pre-cleaner, explicitly to be hot-swapped for the terrain. Torqit is the opposite extreme: the mouth is a 180-degree hairpin formed in the same one-piece mandrel-bent pipe, so there is nothing to rotate and nothing to remove. Mega Jimny has no head at all - just a louvred faceplate screwed to the pillar housing.

The biggest obstacle to modelling these: almost no snorkel maker publishes a dimension. Across every brand in this file the only published numbers are Bravo's 89 mm head, 79x38x16 cm box and 3 kg; Torqit's 3.5 in tube and 2 mm wall; Mega Jimny's 2 in pipework; and URNIETA's factory drawing UN-JIMNY-FB-006 (1048 mm long x 675 mm tall). HEIGHT ABOVE THE FENDER LINE, STAND-OFF FROM THE A-PILLAR and BEND RADII are NOT PUBLISHED by anybody for any product. Every such figure here is a photo-scaled estimate, individually marked ESTIMATED with its reasoning and its scale reference.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON SALE IN TAIWAN, swept 2026-09-22 across Ruten's API, PChome's API, Yahoo TW auctions and BigGo (which aggregates Shopee + Yahoo + Ruten + PChome + Rakuten TW + Coupang). The market splits into four price bands. (1) NT$2,250-4,069 - the unbranded Chinese copy of the TJM Airtec moulding. About 40 Ruten sellers plus Shopee and Yahoo, all the same item, none publishing a diameter, material or head type; 74 hits for 「JB74 呼吸管」 and 83 for 「Jimny 呼吸管」 are essentially all this one product. (2) NT$5,600-8,350 - small Taiwanese shops: 雲林連合吉普's ABS unit at NT$5,600 collected / NT$6,500 fitted, and JIMNY74風格選物's 免鑽孔 one at NT$8,350. (3) NT$10,000-18,000 - Taiwanese HAND-MADE FRP snorkels, 巴西式樣 (Brazilian pattern), black gelcoat, made in Taiwan, shipped with a 1:1 hole template: 機油倉庫 NT$10,000 (Yahoo) / NT$10,600 (Shopee) plus NT$3,500 fitting, 南國吉米 NT$10,500, and tien0811 of 臺中烏日 at NT$12,000-18,000 with colour options including yellow. These are the only Taiwanese-MADE snorkels for this car. (4) NT$14,000-18,800 - the two genuine imports: URNIETA Salado at NT$14,000 (GOAT Wild explorer, 南投名間) and the Spanish Bravo SSJN at NT$18,800 through MRK 4X4, who re-badge it JB072. NOT sold in Taiwan at all: Ironman ISNORKEL070 (a Ruten search for 「Ironman 涉水喉」 returns zero), TJM Airtec, Torqit/ARB, Mega Jimny, and of course Safari - though Ruten does carry Safari snorkels for OTHER vehicles at NT$39,330-87,400, which is what a genuine Safari would cost here. Two more things a configurator should know. (a) THE CHINESE GENERICS TRACE TO ONE SOURCE: the product photos carry the watermark of 廣州杜克汽車配件有限公司 and a 1688 shop URL, with 4WDUNITY and 廣塑塑料 GS as rebadges. They come in TWO body designs - design A, a flat one-piece body hugging the pillar with the forward square-mesh intake MOULDED IN at the top and a second hex-mesh panel low on the body; and design B, a round tube with a SEPARATE rotatable hex-mesh ram head copying the Ironman head, around NT$2,492-3,192. The box holds the body, a blue or black corrugated hose, a 90-degree elbow, three stainless clamps, a short connector, one bracket and hardware. (b) THE NT$625-780 LISTINGS ARE FAKE PRICES - 27 of them. The same sellers list 662 / 2,750 / 3,182 against identical photos of the same complete kit, and NT$662 is about RMB 150, exactly the 1688 wholesale price, so the dropship feed is republishing the RMB figure unconverted. Do not use them as a price floor. (c) momo and PChome carry NO car snorkels at all - both searches return diving gear. (d) Cyclone pre-cleaner heads (蘑菇頭 / 冬菇頭 / 集沙杯) are sold loose in Taiwan at NT$310-670 in 3" and 3.5", with 76 / 90 / 101 mm elements - a cheap head-swap option worth carrying as a separate configurator state. (e) Two Taiwanese listings are NOT snorkels and should not be counted: 泰山美研社 NT$4,800 (料號 22030320) is an INTAKE PIPE for a car that already has a snorkel, and JW WORKS NT$1,250 is an intake cover that fits onto an existing head.

The Taiwanese FRP snorkels at NT$10,000-18,000 describe themselves as 巴西式樣 - 'Brazilian pattern'. That is a real lineage, not a flourish: the BigJimny channel's JB74 snorkel series describes its own kit as 'based on the elusive official Suzuki "Brazilian" snorkel', a factory-accessory snorkel Suzuki sold in Brazil for the Jimny. I could not reach a Suzuki Brazil catalogue page for the original's part number or photo (suzukiveiculos.com.br returned HTTP 500), so the original's exact shape is an open gap. What the Taiwanese sellers do publish is enough to say the copies are hand-laid FRP (fibreglass), black gelcoat, and that they cut the guard - one seller ships a 1:1 paper cutting template in the box.

The cheap unbranded JB74 snorkels are copies of the TJM AIRTEC moulding, not of anything Mitsubishi. Taiwanese listings say so outright: 「涉水喉 jb74 jb64 tjm 版本改裝件」. 'Mitsubishi-style' snorkels are a SEPARATE product line - Pajero V33/V43/V73 and Triton/L200 patterns, themselves copies of the Safari SS66x series - and they are not JB74 parts. If a seller offers a 'Mitsubishi style' snorkel for a Jimny, it is a universal body being cross-listed, not a JB74-specific kit. The tell on a photo is the grille face: Ironman's carries a lattice with its logo, the TJM-pattern copies are plain and unbadged.

families.label: Australian ram-head plastic
families.silhouette: Textured black moulded tube out of the guard top, up the A-pillar standing 40-60 mm proud of it, a band-clamp ring about a third of the way up, then a forward goose-neck carrying a rectangular grille-faced scoop above the roofline. This is the shape most people picture when they hear 'snorkel'.

families.label: One-piece stainless hairpin
families.silhouette: Constant 88.9 mm bright or satin-black round pipe, no head part at all, ending in a 180-degree candy-cane at roof height with the mouth pointing back and slightly down. Reads as a flattened J laid against the body.

families.label: European rotomould with a clamped elbow head
families.silhouette: Wide flat foot along the fender top, a sweeping riser that narrows to a true 89 mm circular spigot, then a separate 90-degree elbow head clamped on and aimed forward.

families.label: No-cut panel replacement
families.silhouette: Barely breaks the stock profile. URNIETA swaps the hood-edge garnish strip for a ducted one and puts a drum head on the pillar top; Mega Jimny swaps the A-pillar trim for a moulding with a louvred faceplate and hides the pipe entirely. Neither projects above the roofline.

families.label: Taiwanese FRP 'Brazilian pattern'
families.silhouette: Hand-laid fibreglass, thicker-walled and squarer-shouldered than a rotomoulded plastic one, usually with a simple forward-facing box scoop. Sold in colours as well as black because FRP is gelcoated or painted, not moulded in colour - tien0811 lists a yellow one.

families.label: Cyclone pre-cleaner head
families.silhouette: A squat drum, Ø180 mm for the 89 mm fitting, roughly as tall as it is wide: black domed lid over a clear polycarbonate bowl, air entering through the annular gap between them and dust spinning down into the visible bowl. Replaces the ram head on the same 89 mm spigot, so it is a head swap on an existing body, not a different snorkel.

products.mostLikelyExplanation: The owner's snorkel is most likely a Taiwanese SHOP-MADE unit bought from a shop or a club contact, and 「怪獸」 is the shop's or the group's informal name rather than a product brand. Taiwan really does have shop-made JB74 snorkels at NT$8,350-18,000 - the FRP 巴西式樣 one (tw_frp_brazilian), the Taichung tien0811 one in colours (tw_tien0811), the 南國吉米 one (tw_south_jimny) and the 免鑽孔 one (tw_jimny74) - and none of them names its manufacturer. Any of those could be the car's snorkel. The only way to settle it is to ask the owner for a photo or the shop's name.

It is a different company, it is Japanese not Taiwanese, and no MONSTER SPORT JB74 snorkel was found - their JB74 catalogue is exhausts, suspension, aero and wheels. Its manual is Portuguese and headed '...TECH' with an 'HPE' footer, but rtech.com.br is under construction and no HPE domain resolves, so the maker is unidentified - and the Taiwanese listing's 產地:台灣 contradicts the Brazilian paperwork. The 公路總局 「涉水管檢驗實務認定標準」 itself. It demonstrably EXISTS - the 交通部 cites it in a written 2023-04-12 reply - but it has never been published: 交通部行政解釋查詢 returns 0 results for both 涉水管 and 呼吸管, it is not in 附件十五, and VSCC does not list it. There is no document number an owner could quote to an inspector.

The three Taiwanese 免鑽孔／免外觀切割 claims - the NT$2,380 and NT$8,350 Shopee listings and 希琦's Bravo copy - are all unverified, and the 希琦 one contradicts Bravo's own installation guide. Do not repeat any of them as fact.
Whether MRK's 「BravoSnorkel Jimny 專用呼吸管 JB072」 at NT$18,800 is the JB74 SSJN or Bravo's part for an older Jimny. The title does not say JB74.
Whether 雲林連合吉普's NT$5,600 ABS unit is a JB74 part at all - the title omits JB74 and the photo is an older-generation shape.

THE 怪獸 PRODUCT ITSELF. No Taiwanese brand by that name makes a JB74 snorkel - see the guaishou_tw entry for everything that was searched and what 怪獸 actually turns out to be in Taiwan. The gap can only be closed by the owner: a photo of the car, or the name of the shop that fitted it.

Shopee TW product DESCRIPTIONS. Shopee returns HTTP 403 to curl, to WebFetch and to its own PDP API for any non-browser client. Every Shopee price in this file came from BigGo's republished listing data; not one Shopee description could be read. That is why four Taiwanese products (tien0811, 南國吉米, JIMNY74風格選物, JW WORKS) have almost no specification. A browser session would close this.
The original Suzuki Brazil 'Brazilian' snorkel. suzukiveiculos.com.br returned HTTP 500, so the factory accessory that the Taiwanese FRP copies descend from has no part number, price or photo here.

TJM Airtec geometry and head type. tjm.com.au, tjm.co.nz and tjm4x4.com are all Cloudflare-blocked; every TJM figure here is from a European dealer, and the head type, side, diameter and bend count are all NOT PUBLISHED anywhere reachable.

Ironman's fitting instructions. Ironman links a generic fitting-instructions index with no per-part PDF exposed, so the guard cut, the template and the airbox grommet contents for ISNORKEL070 are inference rather than published fact.
Height above the fender line and stand-off from the A-pillar, for EVERY product. No maker publishes either figure. All of them here are photo-scaled estimates.
Bend radii and exact bend angles. Not published by anyone. The bend descriptions here are read from fitted photographs.
Mega Jimny publishes no dimensions at all beyond the 2 in pipework; the 95 x 255 mm faceplate is a +/-25% photo estimate under heavy perspective.
Donaldson cyclone BOWL diameters. Donaldson publishes the neck size (89 / 102 mm) but not the bowl OD; the 180 mm figure here is the generic equivalent at the same neck size.
TJM, Ironman and Turbo II cyclone pre-cleaner part numbers. Donaldson's are verified; the others were not reachable.

Four more snorkel makers surfaced but were not verified: MASTERFOREST (France, 'MONTAGE SNORKEL MF JIMNY 2018'), AVC 4X4 (Turkey), X-CAR (3-door and 5-door kits), and Legendex. None is sold in Taiwan and none was confirmed against a maker page.

Whether URNIETA's no-cut install uses only existing holes. The maker says no fender cut, but step 2 screws the body to the fender with supplied screws and clips, and the maker does not say whether those holes already exist.

corrections.target: parts.js SNORKELS id 'precleaner' - fitment and price
corrections.claim: 'Ø180 透明旋風碗' with price null, and the URL slug implying it fits 3-inch snorkels.
corrections.truth: Ø180 and the clear cyclone bowl are CORRECT - and 180 mm is correct specifically for an 89 mm neck. But the fitment is 3.5 INCH (89 mm), not 3 inch; the URL slug reads 'for-3-snorkels' only because the .5" was stripped when the slug was generated, and the page itself says 3.5". corrections.claim: '2 吋不鏽鋼細管貼 A 柱、後向小進氣口；免鑽孔、幾乎看不見' (2-inch stainless slim tube hugging the A-pillar, small rearward-facing intake, no drilling, nearly invisible).
corrections.truth: Two errors inside a mostly-right description. (1) THE INTAKE IS NOT REARWARD-FACING. It is a louvred faceplate set flush into the OUTBOARD face of a housing at the top of the A-pillar - a tall rounded rectangle, colour-matched to the car, four stainless dome screws, with 'MEGA JIMNY' pierced through it; air enters sideways through the slots and the lettering. (2) THERE IS NO VISIBLE TUBE. The 2-inch 304 stainless pipework is real but it is CONCEALED inside a black textured moulded plastic body and under the guard; what you see on the car is a trim moulding in the windscreen/A-pillar channel, not a slim tube. 'No drilling' and 'almost invisible' are both CORRECT and the maker is emphatic about it - 'absolutely NO drilling or holes... completely reversible' - so the earlier claim in docs/jb74-accessory-atlas.json that 'the fender panel still has to be cut' is refuted by the maker's own copy and should be removed. Current version is V4; JB64 is not compatible.

'No huge holes in your front guard/A-pillar here!'... 'completely reversible'. It is a full panel-replacement system and the A-pillar bracket is double-sided tape. Nothing is cut.
